evidence.ref: plugin/templates/scripts/runners/perf/warp_perf_runner.py exists: reads a load journey (name, workload + workload_args, requests, concurrency, budgets of latency percentiles/throughput/error rate), drives the workload requests times across concurrency worker threads (ThreadPoolExecutor), measures each request's latency and whether it raised, computes p50/p95/p99/max, throughput (successful req per wall-clock second) and error rate, checks them against the budgets, exits 0 when every budget holds and 1 with each breached budget named. The workload is a seam: run() takes workload=callable; the reference ships deterministic built-ins (noop, sleep, flaky) selected by name. proof/WARP-0304/runner-evidence.txt: pass fixture exit 0, fail fixture exit 1

assumptions: Reference runner: generic, stdlib only (concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor). No real network target and no external load-generation tooling; the workload is a provider seam, a callable workload(request_index) that raises to signal a failed request. The reference ships deterministic built-in workloads (noop, sleep, flaky) so the concurrency orchestration, the percentile math, and the budget assertions are gate-tested with no external target, and an adopting repo passes its own workload unchanged. The fixtures keep the gate deterministic by construction: generous latency + throughput budgets that hold on any machine, and a zero error budget breached by an index-chosen failure fraction, so pass/fail never depend on wall-clock timing. Shipped under plugin/templates/scripts/runners/perf/; not wired into the warp repo's own gate (capabilities: reference).
